name: Thromboangiitis Obliterans

criteria.description: Current or recent history of tobacco use
Exclusion of autoimmune diseases, hypercoagulable states, and diabetes mellitus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met including age of onset, tobacco use, distal extremity involvement, and exclusion of other diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by angiographic findings; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe pain at rest due to ischemia
searchTerms: pain in fingers or toes at rest from poor blood flow
rest pain in hands or feet

pathognomonic.notes: Ischemic tissue necrosis of fingers or toes
searchTerms: ulcers and tissue death on fingers or toes

common.symptomName: Intermittent claudication of hands or feet
common.notes: Pain during exertion due to arterial insufficiency
searchTerms: cramping pain in hands or feet when walking

common.notes: Exacerbation of symptoms in cold environments
searchTerms: hands and feet get cold easily

common.notes: Diminished or absent pulses distal to occlusion
searchTerms: weak or absent pulses in arms or legs

common.notes: Color changes due to ischemia and reperfusion
searchTerms: skin color changes like paleness or blueness

occasional.notes: Vasospasm of digital arteries triggered by cold
searchTerms: fingers turn white or blue when cold

occasional.notes: Due to chronic ischemia and disuse
searchTerms: muscle wasting in affected arms or legs
loss of muscle bulk in limbs

rare.notes: Rare venous thrombosis in affected limbs
searchTerms: blood clot in deep leg vein
deep vein blood clot causing swelling

rare.notes: Severe ischemic necrosis leading to spontaneous digit loss
searchTerms: fingers or toes falling off spontaneously

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
imaging: Angiography showing segmental occlusions and corkscrew collaterals in distal arteries
Doppler ultrasound demonstrating reduced blood flow in affected vessels
other: Histopathology shows segmental inflammation and thrombosis of small and medium arteries and veins

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes)
Diffuse arterial involvement rather than segmental
Multisystem involvement including renal and hematologic
Lack of strong association with tobacco use
Vasospastic episodes without occlusive arterial disease
Usually no tissue necrosis or ulcerations
Often associated with connective tissue diseases

redFlags: Severe rest pain refractory to analgesics
Signs of critical limb ischemia (pallor, coldness, absent pulses)
references: Olin JW. Thromboangiitis obliterans (Buerger's disease). N Engl J Med. 2000;343(12):864-9.
